source_text: Quid Manichaeus dicit? Per concupiscentiam corporum auctor diabolus est; per hanc diabolus corpora, non animas aucupatur; tolle - inquit - malignae stirpis radicem et spiritalis fies; de hac Apostolus clamat ad Romanos: " Non bonum quod volo, sed malum operor quod exhorreo " [n225] . Nos etiam stultos vocat, qui dicamus figmentum hoc corporis ad Deum pertinere, quod per con cupiscentiam generatum esse fateamur. Vides ergo, quanta tibi sit et Manichaeo in nostri impugnatione concordia; eius dimicas verbis, eius niteris argumentis et nos mentiri dicis, qui te discipulum illius non solum fuisse, ut ipse scribis, sed etiam esse dicamus. Et in hoc tamen ille prudentior, qui, cum hanc concupiscentiam carnis a diabolo credidisset immissam, collegit confitendum esse ad Dei operam non pertinere, quidquid de diabolica concupiscentia appareret prolatum.
pass_a_gloss: What does the Manichaean say? Through desire the author of bodies is the devil; through this the devil snares bodies, not souls; take away, he says, the root of the malign stock and you will become spiritual; of this the Apostle cries to the Romans: Not the good which I will, but I work the evil which I abhor. He also calls us stupid, who say this figment of the body pertains to God, which we confess generated through desire. You see therefore how great a concord there is to you and the Manichaean in the impugnation of us; you fight by his words, you strive by his arguments, and you say we lie, who say you not only have been his disciple, as you yourself write, but even are. And in this nevertheless he more prudent, who, when he had believed this desire of the flesh sent in by the devil, collected that it must be confessed not to pertain to the work of God, whatever appeared brought forth from diabolical desire.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: What does Mani say? ‘The devil creates bodies through desire. Through it he snares bodies, not souls. Remove the root of evil stock,’ he says, ‘and you will become spiritual. About this the apostle cries to the Romans: “I do not do the good I want, but I perform the evil I abhor”’ (Romans 7:19). He also calls us foolish for saying that this bodily formation belongs to God, although we acknowledge that it was generated through desire.

You see, then, how fully you and Mani agree in attacking us. You fight with his words, rely on his arguments, and call us liars for saying you not only were his disciple, as you yourself write, but still are. Yet even here he is more sensible. Believing this fleshly desire was introduced by the devil, he concluded that whatever appeared produced from diabolical desire must be acknowledged not to belong to God’s work.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
